description: The line plot illustrates the performance of two different models, GPT-4o and Claude-3.5-Sonnet, in terms of their pass@1 rate percentage as a function of the number of reasoning steps. The x-axis is labeled "Num. of Reasoning Steps" and is a linear scale ranging from 0 to 40, with tick labels at intervals of 5. The y-axis is labeled "Pass@1 Rate (%)" and is a linear scale ranging from 0 to 100, with tick labels at intervals of 20. The line representing GPT-4o is marked with a solid line and circular markers, while the line representing Claude-3.5-Sonnet is marked with a dashed line and 'x' markers. The GPT-4o line starts at a pass@1 rate of 6.5% at 5 reasoning steps, increases to 19.4% at 10 steps, then to 38.7% at 20 steps, and finally to 89.2% at 40 steps. The Claude-3.5-Sonnet line starts at a pass@1 rate of 6.5% at 5 reasoning steps, increases to 32.3% at 10 steps, then to 77.4% at 20 steps, and finally to 83.9% at 40 steps. The plot shows that both models improve their performance as the number of reasoning steps increases, with GPT-4o consistently outperforming Claude-3.5-Sonnet at each point.
